chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

‘Everything whose origin is in the sea and is found in both the land and the sea, it is not befitting for the one in Ihram to kill it. So if he kills it, then upon him is the penalty, just as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said.’
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim in Ihram who kills a sea creature that also lives on land?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the status of amphibious creatures (like turtles and frogs) for a Muhrim, distinguishing them from pure sea fish by ruling that killing them incurs a penalty (damm) similar to land game, as they share characteristics of both realms. Scholars note this ruling highlights the principle of 'fitrah' (natural state) and the precautionary measure taken by the Imams to preserve marine life during pilgrimage, linking the penalty directly to the Quranic verse in Surah Al-Ma'idah. The reference to 'as stated by Allah' underscores the divine origin of this specific jurisprudential distinction within Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Everything whose origin happens to be in the sea and happens to be in the land and the sea, so it is not befitting of the one in Ihraam that he should kill it. So if he were to kill it, then upon him would be the penalty, just as Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Said’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘ Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Everything that originates from the sea but is found on land and in the sea, on the basis of precaution, should not be killed by those who are in the state of Ihram. If they kill such animals, they owe penalty as Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has said.’”
